questions.q: An ideal monatomic gas is confined in a cylinder by a spring-loaded massless piston of cross-section $8 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{2}$. The piston can slide on the walls of the cylinder without any friction. Initially, the gas is at $300K$ and occupies a volume of $2.4 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$ and the spring is in its relaxed position. Now, gas is slowly heated by a small electric heater and the piston moves out slowly by $0.1 m$. Calculate the final temperature of the gas and the heat supplied by the heater. The force constant of the spring is $8000N / m$ and atmospheric pressure is $1 \times {10}^{5}N / m^{2}$.
questions.solution:
In the initial condition

${P}_{1} = {10}^{5}Pa$, ${V}_{1} = 2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$, ${T}_{1} = 300K$

Finally,

${P}_{2} = {P}_{1} + \dfrac{kx}{A} = 2 \times {10}^{5}Pa$

${V}_{2} = {V}_{1} + Ax = 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$

$\dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{T1} = \dfrac{{P}_{2}{V}_{2}}{T2}$, on solving we get

${T}_{2} = 800K$

Applying work-energy theorem for the piston

${W}_{gas} + {W}_{atmos} + {W}_{spring} = 0$

${W}_{gas} = {P}_{0}Ax + \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = 120J$

$\Delta U = n{C}_{V} \Delta T = nR \Delta T\left(\gamma - 1\right) = {P}_{2}{V}_{2} - {P}_{1}{V}_{1}\left(\gamma - 1\right) = 600J$

$Q = \Delta U + {W}_{gas} = 600 + 120 = 720J$

questions.q: A Carnot engine has efficiency $\dfrac{1}{5}$. Efficiency becomes $\dfrac{1}{3}$ when the temperature of sink is decreased by $50K$. Temperature of the sink ( in $K$ ) is
questions.solution:
The efficiency of the Carnot engine

$η = \dfrac{Workoutput}{Heatinput} = \dfrac{W}{{Q}_{H}}$

or $η = \dfrac{{Q}_{H} - {Q}_{L}}{{Q}_{H}} = 1 - \dfrac{{Q}_{L}}{{Q}_{H}}$

Also we can show that

$\dfrac{{Q}_{L}}{{Q}_{H}} = \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$

$∴ η = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$

where ${T}_{L}$ is temperature of sink and ${T}_{H}$ is the temperature of hot reservoir.

According to question

$\dfrac{1}{5} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$ ...($i$)

$\dfrac{1}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L} - 50}{{T}_{H}}$ ...($ii$)

From Eq. ($i$)

$\dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$⇒ {T}_{H} = \dfrac{5}{4}{T}_{L}$

Substituting value of ${T}_{H}$ in Eq. ($ii$), we get

$\dfrac{1}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L} - 50}{\dfrac{5}{4}{T}_{L}}$

$or\dfrac{4 ( {T}_{L} - 50 )}{5{T}_{L}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$or{T}_{L} - 50 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{4}{T}_{L}$

$or{T}_{L} - \dfrac{5}{6}{T}_{L} = 50$

$∴ {T}_{L} = 50 \times 6 = 300K$

questions.q: A gas mixture consists of $2$ moles of oxygen and $4$ moles of argon at temperature $T$. Neglecting all vibrational modes we calculated the total internal energy of the system to be $xRT$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution:
The internal energy of n moles of a gas is $U = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{nFRT}$
where F = number of degrees of freedom.
The internal energy of 2 moles of oxygen at temperature T is

${\text{U}}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 5\text{RT} = 5\text{RT}$ (F = 5 for oxygen molecule)

The total internal energy of 4 moles of argon at temperature T is

${U}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3\text{RT} = 6\text{RT}$ (F = 3 for argon molecule)

Total internal energy $= {U}_{1} + {U}_{2} = 11\text{RT}$

$⇒ x = 11$

questions.q: $N$ moles of an ideal diatomic gas is enclosed in a cylinder at temperature $T$. suppose on supplying heat to the gas, its temperature remains constant but $n$ moles get dissociated into atoms. Heat supplied to the gas is
questions.solution:
Since the gas is enclosed in a vessel, therefore, during heating process, volume of the gas remains constant. Hence, no work is done by the gas. It means heat supplied to the gas is used to increase its internal energy only.

Initial internal energy of the gas is ${U}_{1} = \text{N} \left(\dfrac{5}{2} \text{R}\right) \text{T}$

Since n moles get dissociated into atoms, therefore, after heating, vessel contains $\left(\text{N} - \text{n}\right)$~ moles of diatomic gas and 2n moles of a mono-atomic gas. Hence, the heat supplied = increase in internal energy

$= \left({U}_{2} - {U}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{nRT}$

questions.q: A Carnot engine has efficiency $\dfrac{1}{5}$. Efficiency becomes $\dfrac{1}{3}$ when the temperature of sink is decreased by $50K$. What is the temperature of the sink (in $K$)?
questions.solution:
The efficiency of Carnot engine

$η = \dfrac{Workoutput}{Heatinput} = \dfrac{W}{{Q}_{H}}$

or $η = \dfrac{{Q}_{H} - {Q}_{L}}{{Q}_{H}} = 1 - \dfrac{{Q}_{L}}{{Q}_{H}}$

Also we can show that

$\dfrac{{Q}_{L}}{{Q}_{H}} = \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$

$∴ η = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$

where ${T}_{L}$ is temperature of sink and ${T}_{H}$ is temperature of hot reservoir.

According to question

$\dfrac{1}{5} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$ ...(i)

$and\dfrac{1}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L} - 50}{{T}_{H}}$ ...(ii)

From Eq. (i)

$\dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$⇒ {T}_{H} = \dfrac{5}{4}{T}_{L}$

Substituting value of ${T}_{H}$ in Eq. (ii), we get

$\dfrac{1}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L} - 50}{\dfrac{5}{4}{T}_{L}}$

$or\dfrac{4 ( {T}_{L} - 50 )}{5{T}_{L}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$or{T}_{L} - 50 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{4}{T}_{L}$

$or{T}_{L} - \dfrac{5}{6}{T}_{L} = 50$

$∴ {T}_{L} = 50 \times 6 = 300K$

questions.q: The diagram shows a horizontal cylindrical container of length $30cm$, which is partitioned by a tight-fitting separator. The separator is diathermic but conducts heat very slowly. Initially the separator is in equilibrium. As heat is conducted from the right to left part, separator displaces to the right. Find the displacement of separator (in $cm$) after a long when gases on the two parts of the cylinder are in thermal equilibrium.
questions.solution:
It is given that initially, the separator is in equilibrium; thus pressure on both sides of the gas is equal say, it is Pi. If A be the area of cross-section of cylinder, number of moles of gas in the left and right part, n1 and n2, can be given as

${n}_{1} = \dfrac{{P}_{\text{i}}\left(10\text{A}\right)}{R\left(100\right)}$

and ${n}_{2} = \dfrac{{P}_{\text{i}}\left(20\text{A}\right)}{R\left(400\right)}$

Finally, if the separator is displaced to right by a distance x,
we have

${n}_{1} = \dfrac{{\text{P}}_{f ⁡ \text{i}}\left(10 + \text{x}\right)\text{A}}{{\text{RT}}_{f ⁡}}$

and ${\text{n}}_{2} = \dfrac{{\text{P}}_{f ⁡}\left(20 - \text{x}\right)\text{A}}{{\text{RT}}_{f ⁡}}$

Here ${\text{P}}_{f ⁡}$ and ${\text{T}}_{f ⁡}$ are the final pressure and temperature on both sides after a long time.
Now if we equate the ratio of moles n1/n2 in initial and final states, we get

$\dfrac{{\text{n}}_{1}}{{\text{n}}_{2}} = \dfrac{\left(10\text{A} / 100\right)}{\left(20\text{A} / 400\right)} = \dfrac{\left(10 + \text{x}\right)\text{A}}{\left(20 - \text{x}\right)\text{A}}$

$2\left(20 - \text{x}\right) = 10 + \text{x}$

$\text{x} = 10 cm$

Thus in the final state when gases in both parts are in thermal equilibrium, the piston is displaced 10 cm rightward from its initial position.
